_what: verification that the code ported into this repo reproduces the recorded Table 3 configuration on a GPU, and a fresh base-model PB measurement

steering_paper_point.config: lambda=0.02 mu=0.5 n=64 seed=0 sample_steps=100 mfm_steps=10 value_samples=4 guide_every=2 t in [0.1,0.9], EMA teacher, targets filter
steering_paper_point.interpretation: Guided sampling is not bit-reproducible (non-deterministic CUDA backward) and TF32 matmuls differ between GPU generations, so none of the three runs matches another exactly -- the authors' own rerun of the unchanged script already moved the unguided arm 0.2072 -> 0.2100 and the gain 0.0199 -> 0.0156. The ported code lands in the same range (unguided within 0.005 of both earlier runs) and its gain is 1.5 paired SEM from the recorded one. At n=64 the gain itself is ~1.9 SEM from zero, so these runs do not separate the port from the original, nor the effect from noise; the n=4,096 x 3 evaluation is the discriminating measurement.

base_model_pb_validity.note: first measurement of the released base checkpoint under the GEOM PB configuration used by Table 3/21. 88.0% at N=100 is consistent with the 87.5% (N=64) and 88.0% (N=4,096x3) unguided arms of the steering runs, and not with Table 21's 92.0%. N=100 is small; NUM_SAMPLES=4096 sbatch scripts/geom/eval_pb_validity.sbatch settles it.
